On November 19, the leaders of China, the United States and Russia will gather for a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen on the sidelines of an annual Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. The three have never met for formal trilateral talks, and some commentators are already calling the meeting “historic”. In Moscow, many observers see the gathering as a “new Yalta” – another conference to divide the world into spheres of influence, similar to the one held in 1945 between Britain, the USSR and the US. This thinking reflects Russian President Vladimir Putin’s own worldview. It is perhaps unsurprising that he was the one to propose the trilateral meeting during a call with US President Donald Trump in October. A “new Yalta”, however, appears to be more of a case of wishful thinking than a realistic possibility. In 1945, the Soviet Union, the US and Britain came together after emerging victorious from the second world war, in which they fought against a common enemy. Today, not only do they find themselves on opposing sides of various conflicts and disputes, but they also seem to disagree on how the world should run. While all three powers speak of a new, multipolar world and formally reject the language of hegemony, they seem to have divergent understandings of what that means. Moscow, for example, seeks to establish itself as one of the poles in a multipolar world and a regional leader in Eurasia. Washington, on the other hand, wants to secure its status as the pre-eminent power, while Beijing remains preoccupied with pulling the Global South away from US leadership. Therefore, the US and China are championing a bipolar system – a world shaped by the “G2” as Trump calls it – which Russia might be unhappy with but has no means of stopping. This disparity of aspirations is also apparent at the economic level. Five years ago, Anthropic raised $124m from its first investors. On Wednesday, it priced its shares at $83 each, valuing the company at roughly $1.5 trillion and making it the world’s 12th-biggest company, just behind Tesla. Its shares begin trading on the Nasdaq in New York on Thursday under the ticker “ANT”. Demand far outstripped expectations. Investors reportedly sought six times as many shares as were available, and Anthropic sold 980 million shares, up from the 825 million it had planned, at a price above its expected range of $70 to $78. An initial public offering (IPO) is the process by which a private company sells shares to the public for the first time by listing on a stock exchange. The company raises money by issuing new shares, and existing owners, such as founders and early investors, can sell some of theirs. To prepare, the company hires investment banks to value it and run the sale. The banks write a prospectus explaining its business, finances and risks. Executives and bankers then pitch the shares to big investors to gauge demand before setting the price. Early investors are usually barred from selling for several months after the listing. Anthropic was founded in 2021 by seven former OpenAI employees, including siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei. It develops AI models under its Claude brand, making most of its money by selling businesses access. Its growth has been extraordinary. clusters.text: Critics hail GTA 6 as a ‘masterpiece’, ‘spectacular’, and an ‘astonishing American epic’. Grand Theft Auto VI has launched to rave reviews, in one of the most hotly anticipated releases in gaming history. Gamers got their hands on the latest instalment of the GTA franchise on Thursday, as critics hailed the open-world game as a “masterpiece”, “spectacular”, and an “astonishing American epic”. The immersive game had an aggregate score of 99 out of 100 on Metacritic, based on more than 150 reviews, as it began dropping on game consoles worldwide from midnight. “Exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played,” critic Luke Reilly wrote in a gushing review for gaming website IGN. “Accepting that GTA 6 is very much not real also makes it all the more astonishing how much the game is very real,” reviewer Jordan Minor wrote in PCMag. Grand Theft Auto VI follows the exploits of Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, a Bonnie and Clyde-like duo who become entangled in a criminal conspiracy after a seemingly easy score goes awry. Players have free rein to explore the hyper-realistic fictional state of Leonida and its coastal metropolis of Vice City, stand-ins for Florida and Miami. Like previous entries in the series, Grand Theft Auto VI features graphic depictions of crime and violence, with players able to mow down pedestrians in stolen vehicles and engage in shootouts with police. The game, developed by New York-based Rockstar Games at an estimated cost of more than $1bn, is the first instalment in the series since the release of Grand Theft Auto V in 2013. Originally set to go on sale in 2025, the release was delayed twice to allow developers to polish up gameplay. Grand Theft Auto VI, which is available on the PlayStation 5 and the Xbox Series, is likely to be the most lucrative release in the history of the gaming industry, which is projected to be worth as much as $350bn by the end of the decade. Pre-orders for Grand Theft Auto VI exceeded an estimated 15.8 million units as of November 17, generating $1.54bn in revenue, according to the market intelligence platform Sensor Tower. The GTA series began in 1997 with the launch of Grand Theft Auto, a 2D top-down open-world game available on the personal computer, PlayStation and Game Boy Color.

clusters.text: BENGALURU: Puneeth M is no stranger to success at the U-14 level. The Bengaluru boy has already won six Asian Tennis Federation singles titles, among other achievements. But his ambitions extend beyond this circuit; he has set his sights on stepping up to a higher level next season.After winning the U-14 boys’ singles and doubles events at the Fenesta Open in New Delhi last month, Puneeth did not rest on his laurels. He began his off-season training a couple of days later, primarily to prepare for the ITF junior circuit in 2027.He is aware of the task ahead and has been working on his strength and stamina to compete against older players. The 14-year-old, who stands at 5ft 8in, puts in five hours of work every day, covering fitness and tennis, six days a week."I am expecting older boys (than me) to have more experience. They'll be physically tougher to play against. That's a step up for me. I am working vigorously to develop my body and make myself stronger physically for the next level," said Puneeth, who played in the 14 & Under Wimbledon Championships in July. Competing against better players made Puneeth, who trains at the Transform Tennis Academy in Hennur under coach Prashanth Selvaraj, realise the need to improve his game.He possesses a strong serve and is not afraid to step in and work his way to the net. He is also working on becoming more aggressive."Slowly he is transitioning from a grinder to an aggressive player. We are consciously working towards that. clusters.text: Prayagraj: Nearly 63,000 voters have been added to Prayagraj district’s electoral rolls since the final voter list was published on April 10, taking the total electorate to 39,28,598 ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections.District magistrate and district election officer Manish Kumar Verma announced the figures during the publication of the draft electoral rolls on Tuesday and said another opportunity would now be available to eligible voters to get their names added to the rolls.The final electoral roll published on April 10 had around 38.65 lakh voters, while the draft roll now has 39,28,598 voters, comprising 21,46,070 men, 17,82,231 women and 297 third-gender voters.Allahabad West has the highest electorate among the 12 assembly constituencies with 3,79,223 voters, followed by Pratappur with 3,59,927 and Handia with 3,45,740. Allahabad North has the lowest electorate at 2,85,881, followed by Meja with 2,91,845. Third-gender voters have been registered in all constituencies, with Allahabad South having the highest number at 106.Verma said claims and objections against the draft electoral roll would be accepted till Dec 16, with forms available with booth-level officers (BLOs). Those who will attain the age of 18 on Jan 1, 2027, can submit Form 6 to get their names included in the electoral roll. People whose names were deleted during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise because they were found absent or had shifted can also submit Form 6 if they have since returned.
